fn.name: blank
fn.description: An empty grid.

fn.name: width
fn.description: How many cells wide a grid is.

fn.name: height
fn.description: How many cells high a grid is.

fn.name: is_alive
fn.description: yes if the cell at x, y is alive.

fn.name: population
fn.description: How many cells are alive.

fn.name: set_cell
fn.params: grid, x: int, y: int, alive
fn.description: A copy of the grid with one cell made alive or dead.

fn.name: toggle
fn.description: A copy of the grid with one cell flipped.

return.value: @set_cell($grid, x: $x, y: $y, alive: not @is_alive($grid, x: $x, y: $y))

fn.name: place
fn.params: grid, rows, left = null, top = null
fn.description: Draws a pattern onto a grid, centred unless left and top are given. Cells off the edge are dropped.

if.test: $c eq $alive_cell and $x ge 0 and $y ge 0 and $x lt @width($grid) and $y lt @height($grid)

fn.name: random_grid
fn.description: A grid where about density percent of the cells are alive.

fn.name: parse_cells
fn.description: Reads a pattern in the plaintext .cells format: lines of O and ., with ! comment lines. Any of O, o, *, # or X counts as alive.

throw.message: That pattern has no cells in it.

fn.name: neighbours
fn.description: How many of the 8 cells around x, y are alive. With wrap, the edges join up like a torus.

if.test: $nx ge 0 and $ny ge 0 and $nx lt $w and $ny lt $h and $grid[$ny][$nx] eq $alive_cell

fn.name: next_state
fn.description: Conway's rule: a live cell with 2 or 3 neighbours lives on; a dead cell with exactly 3 comes alive.

fn.name: next_generation
fn.description: The next generation of a grid.

fn.name: next_row
fn.description: One row of the next generation, from the rows above and below it.

fn.name: new_world
fn.description: A world at generation 0.

return.value: { grid: $grid, generation: 0, history: [$grid->join('')], wrap: $wrap, pattern: $pattern, births: 0, deaths: 0 }

fn.name: pattern_world
fn.params: name, width: int, height: int, wrap = true
fn.description: A world with a named pattern from $patterns in the middle.

throw.message: There's no pattern called '{$name}'. Try one of: { $patterns->keys()->join(', ') }.

fn.name: edit_world
fn.description: The world with its grid replaced by hand (a click or a typed cell). Starts the history again.

fn.name: flip
fn.description: The world with one cell flipped, where is "column,row" from 0 (what a board button sends). Anything else leaves the world as it is.

if.test: $xy->count() ne 2 or $xy[0] lt 0 or $xy[1] lt 0 or $xy[0] ge @width($world.grid) or $xy[1] ge @height($world.grid)

fn.name: advance
fn.description: Runs a world forward, counting births and deaths and keeping a short history for spotting cycles. Stops early once nothing is left alive.

fn.name: period
fn.description: The length of the cycle the world is in (1 for a still life), or 0 if it hasn't repeated within the history.

fn.name: status
fn.description: A short description of what the world is doing.

fn.name: summary
fn.description: The numbers both front ends show under the grid.

return.value: { generation: $world.generation, population: $pop, density: ($pop / $cells * 100)->round(digits: 1), births: $world.births, deaths: $world.deaths, status: @status($world), size: @width($world.grid) + ' × ' + @height($world.grid), edges: $world.wrap ? 'wrap around' : 'walls' }

fn.name: to_text
fn.description: The grid as lines of text, for terminals and tests.
